title: Week Ahead, Sun 1 Nov: Iran offers a two-day Hormuz reopening plan
description:
Hot topic: Iran floats a two-day plan to reopen Hormuz, but only on its terms, just as Trump's pre-midterm pause on strikes runs out. Then: the Nasdaq's chip rout, Reliance's record quarter, OPEC+, the Nifty's week, the week ahead, Fed hike odds, Apple, India's results week and NTPC.

1. Iran offers a two-day plan to reopen Hormuz as Trump's pre-midterm pause on strikes runs out Tuesday (Al Jazeera; House of Saud)
2. Nasdaq sinks 2.9% to end October as Intel has its worst day since 1974 and AI spending fears hit chips (Reuters via Investing.com; Reuters via WHTC; TheStreet)
3. Reliance's record Rs 29,550 crore Q2 profit meets the market on Monday after a 68% jump in refining earnings (Mint via TradingView; Whalesbook)
4. OPEC+ meets today with Saudi output 2.1 million barrels a day below quota and the strait still closed (House of Saud; CNBC)
5. Nifty gains about 2% for the week and mid and small caps jump as FIIs buy Rs 13,213 crore in October's last week (Outlook Money; Upstox)
6. Week ahead: US midterms Tuesday, India and US PMIs, and US payrolls Friday (Outlook Money; Moneycontrol via TradingView)
7. Fed hike odds near 80% after 3.6% PCE as the 10-year yield drops to 4.93% on the tech rout (Fox Business; Rallies.ai; Newsquawk)
8. Apple reports Monday with the Street at about $113 billion of revenue and $1.98 a share in John Ternus's first call as CEO (If You Spent; StockTitan)
9. SBI, Airtel, M&M, Titan, LIC and ONGC headline a heavy results week (Goodreturns)
10. NTPC's Q2 profit jumps 39% to Rs 7,030 crore on 21% revenue growth; Rs 3 interim dividend (ANI)

From the Ripple news desk. Voices are AI-generated from the hosts' own recordings. This is news, not investment advice; the hosts are not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Good morning, this is Ripple Daily. I'm Pri.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: And I'm SU. Ten stories, under ten minutes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: It's Sunday, so this is our Week Ahead. And the big one: Iran says Hormuz could reopen in two days.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: SU, two days? What happened?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said talks with Qatari mediators produced a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: In September, that roadmap was seven days. But there's a catch: Washington must first accept five conditions.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What is Iran asking for?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Sanctions relief, fewer US forces, oil-export waivers, and released assets.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Security chief Mohsen Rezaei said a letter from JD Vance showed the US tone had changed completely.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And what does Trump say?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: His pledge to hold off strikes before the 3 November midterms expires on Tuesday. He said anything's possible afterwards.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Okay, but it's a list of demands. Why should India care before anyone says yes?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Now, why it matters. January Brent settled at 113.43 dollars on Friday, and India imports most of its oil.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Monday's oil, rupee and fuel retailer moves hinge on whether this reads as a real path to reopening, or terms Washington will reject.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: So what do we watch?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The trigger is Washington's reply. A positive response and Brent opening below 110 dollars would confirm it.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: A rejection, or strikes after Tuesday, could send Brent back toward 117 dollars.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Stocks in focus: BPCL, Indian Oil, IndiGo, and ONGC. Sentiment: mixed.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Rapid fire. Story two: Wall Street ended October on a sour note.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nasdaq fell 2.86% on Friday and the S&P 500 lost 1.82%. Intel fell 28.6% after a weak revenue forecast.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Was it just Intel?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: No. AMD fell 10.9%, and the Philadelphia chip index lost 15.4% in October, its worst month since March 2025.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a chip-led rout sets a risk-off tone for Indian electronics, IT and foreign flows on Monday. Sentiment: negative. Stocks in focus: Dixon, Netweb, Kaynes, TCS.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story three: Reliance's record quarter finally meets the market.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Reliance reported a profit of 29,550 crore rupees, up 34%, after Friday's close. Oil-to-chemicals EBITDA jumped 67.9%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Any weak spot?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Retail. Reliance Retail's profit fell 24.3% to 2,611 crore rupees, on revenue up just 6.4%.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: the Nifty's second-largest stock riding war-time refining margins is direct support for the index. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: Reliance, MRPL, BPCL, HPCL.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story four: OPEC+ meets today. Does it even matter with the strait shut?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Barely. Saudi Arabia pumped about 8.37 million barrels a day in September, roughly 2.1 million below its 10.5 million quota.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The mined strait and Houthi attacks constrain its exports. No analyst cited by House of Saud expects a quota increase.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: once Hormuz reopens, how OPEC+ treats lost supply shapes where oil settles for India. Sentiment: neutral. Stocks in focus: ONGC, Oil India, HPCL.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story five: back home, a good week, and the foreigners came back.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The Nifty rose about 2% for the week to 23,053. The Midcap 100 gained 2.69%, and the Smallcap 100 4%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: But weren't FIIs selling all month?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: They were. Net sales were 34,843 crore rupees in October, but they bought 13,213 crore in the final week.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: foreign buying is what this market lacked all year, and the midterms test whether it lasts. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, TCS.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story six: a packed calendar. Walk me through it.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Monday, India's final manufacturing PMI, with the flash at 54.9, plus US ISM. Tuesday, the US midterms.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Wednesday, India's services PMI, flash 56.2. Thursday, the Bank of England. Friday, US October payrolls.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Anything darker in there?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Outlook Money flags reports that the US and Israel have drawn up plans for possible strikes on Iran after the vote.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: dense data and an election land while markets price a December Fed hike and oil above 110 dollars. Sentiment: mixed. What to watch Monday: India's PMI.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story seven: the Fed could actually hike.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: US PCE inflation came in at 3.6% for September. CME FedWatch put December hike odds at 79.6%.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Yet bond yields fell?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: The 10-year dropped 6.4 basis points to 4.925%, as money fled the chip sell-off. Payrolls are expected at plus 55,000.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: a hiking Fed keeps the dollar firm and foreign flows into India cautious. Sentiment: negative. What to watch: Friday's payrolls.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story eight: Apple reports Monday, with a new CEO on the call.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: It's John Ternus's first call as CEO. Consensus is 1.98 dollars a share, against 1.85 a year ago, on revenue near 113.4 billion dollars.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What's the risk?

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Apple warned memory costs would rise. Its 47 to 48% margin guide includes about 1 point from tariff refunds.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: Apple's iPhone read tests the Asian supply chain, including Indian electronics makers. Sentiment: neutral. Stocks in focus: Dixon, Kaynes.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: Story nine: a heavy results week at home.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: SBI and Bajaj Finserv report Tuesday. Bharti Airtel, Mahindra and Mahindra, Titan, LIC and ONGC on Thursday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Then Hindalco on Friday, and Tata Steel on Saturday.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: six Nifty heavyweights in one week can set the index's direction into Diwali. Sentiment: neutral. Stocks in focus: SBI, Airtel, M&M, Titan.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: And story ten: NTPC surprises.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: NTPC's Q2 profit rose 38.7% to 7,030 crore rupees, on revenue up 21.2%. The board declared a 3 rupee interim dividend.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: Why it matters: India's largest power producer beat its usual mid-teens growth, supporting the power-demand trade. Sentiment: positive. Stocks in focus: NTPC, NTPC Green, JSW Energy, NHPC.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: What to watch Monday: Washington's reply to Iran, Reliance's open, and Apple after the US close.

lines.speaker: SU
lines.text: That's Ripple Daily. Full stories and sources are in the show notes. This is news, not investment advice. We're not SEBI-registered advisers.

lines.speaker: PRI
lines.text: See you tomorrow morning.
